prompt: Show January, February and March 2026 revenue in a table, followed by one brief observation.

answer.markdown:
### Calvin Klein Revenue (Q1 2026)

| Month | Revenue |
| :--- | :--- |
| January 2026 | 125.00 |
| February 2026 | 100.00 |
| March 2026 | 150.00 |

*Note: Figures reflect qualifying sales (excluding cancelled and returned orders/items). Currency is not specified in the source data.*

### Observation
Following a 20% dip in February to 100.00, monthly revenue rebounded by 50% in March to reach a quarterly peak of 150.00.

evidence.sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%B %Y', purchased_at) AS month_label,
  DATE_TRUNC(DATE(purchased_at), MONTH) AS month_date,
  ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS revenue
FROM sales
WHERE brand = 'Calvin Klein'
  AND purchased_at >= '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND purchased_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY month_label, month_date
ORDER BY month_date ASC
evidence.definitions: scoped-retail-v1; sales contains qualifying item purchases, excluding Cancelled/Returned at both item and order level. transactions contains all current statuses. Revenue uses sale_price; orders and customers require distinct IDs. Brand scope applies before joins and history. purchased_at is the item's created_at. Use UTC half-open periods. Current statuses cannot reconstruct historical status changes. Currency is not specified. Customer geography is available only through query_state_summary.
